newsitem.title: JAPAN: Spread trades could enliven Japan stocks - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Spread trades could enliven Japan stocks - brokers.

text.p: Spread trades in Nikkei 225 and TOPIX futures scheduled to start Friday are costly compared to similar trades done on the Singapore Merchantile Exchange (SIMEX) but the introduction is highly welcome, brokers said.
"Osaka bourse spread trade fees are the same as selling and buying back futures (outright) and are expensive compared to SIMEX," said a second-tier brokerage futures dealer.
"But considering the hassle and communications costs of doing trades on SIMEX, domestic spread trading will make the work easier, and this is commendable," he added.

Spread trades involve purchasing one futures contract and simultaneously selling another of a different month to take advantage of price discrepancies. Spread trades in Nikkei 300 futures started in Osaka in April last year.
Spread trading fees for Nikkei 225 futures on SIMEX are much lower than those planned for similar trading on the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE), according to bourse data.
A spokesman at the Tokyo Securities Exchange (TSE) added that taxes were also likely to make spread trading in Japan more costly than in Singapore.
Nevertheless, traders see the launch of spread trading in Nikkei 225 and TOPIX futures as a step toward invigorating the stock market in general.

"Domestic investors, mainly investment trusts and large-lot investors who had taken their business to SIMEX, will be able to come back, which will help revive the market," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.

To accommodate the start of spread trades, futures trading hours will be lengthened by 10 minutes to 3.10 p.m. (0610 GMT). In a bid to breathe more life into stock trading in Japan, both bourses are also planning to start trading in individual stock options, with the OSE aiming for a July 18 start.
Issues will be selected from stocks included in both the Nikkei 225 and Nikkei 300 indices, based on how international they are and what industries they represent.
The Osaka bourse is likely to decide by its next executive meeting on May 20 which shares will be offered
